If you are tired of working with slow-performing apps and looking for the best cloud platforms among AWS vs Azure vs GCP to migrate your essential app and data, then this is the right article for you!

As you know, the migration of a legacy application to the cloud is a rather complex task, but it has become an integral part of business growth and development. Here, the top three cloud service providers, which include AWS, Azure, and GCP, are offering solutions to the migration, integration, and protection of vast amounts of data. However, each of these cloud platforms has its unique features and services, making the selection of one quite complex.

So, let’s compare the three foremost legacy app migration cloud platforms – Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), with a guide to choose the best cloud migration for legacy applications.

Why Legacy Application Migration to Cloud Is Essential Now

Outdated applications still perform many essential business operations. But if you are using old apps, it will cause you to struggle with frequent downtime, missed opportunities, compliance fines, and security issues.

This means not upgrading or replacing these legacy apps, meaning your business may fall behind and hold you back instead of booming.

That’s why the lift and shift of legacy app migration cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and GCP becomes necessary for business growth. This helps you with scalability, improved security, enhanced collaborations, and cost savings.

Beyond cost reduction, transferring data and resources to the cloud allows you access to modern features. This can include handling increased workload demands, helping with serverless computing, microservices architecture, and even modern AI tools and machine learning.

3 Leading Legacy App Migration Cloud Platforms

Integrating legacy application migration to cloud is a necessary element for any business seeking growth in this competitive world. AWS, Azure, and GCP- all the best cloud platforms from which you can build and manage centralized data models and easy workflows and operations within an organization.

Let’s discover Azure, AWS, and GCP and how they are role models in protecting data, simplifying processes, and streamlining business opportunities.

1. AWS (Amazon Web Services)

Amazon has become the largest provider of commercial cloud computing services by offering Amazon Web Services (AWS) to businesses. With its robust infrastructure, numerous services, and cost-effective pricing, businesses can scale their operations over time without worrying about the underlying infrastructure.

Started in 2000 and launched its first service, Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS), in 2003, AWS today is a leading cloud provider, with a wide range of services and a large customer base. This is more adaptable for e-commerce businesses, software development companies, and data-driven businesses.

Its basic features include automated discovery, replication, and testing of apps for migration to the AWS cloud. It has tools like AWS MGN that replicate apps to AWS, further minimize downtime, and make easy assessments, and migrating legacy apps.

2. Microsoft Azure

Azure is another top cloud hosting choice for businesses of all sizes looking for advanced growth and success. Microsoft Azure helps businesses with its legacy migration services that offer big perks like savings in resources and maintenance, along with flexibility, better security, backup, and recovery.

Launched in 2010, today it offers extensive capabilities for migrating large datasets or infrastructure management with round-the-clock support. Now, businesses can enjoy better customer experience, low latency, advanced networking, and optimized routing—wherever they are.

Its easy assessment, migration, modernization, and management of apps to the Azure cloud make it a reliable choice for most business owners.

3. GCP (Google Cloud Platform)

GCP is a suite of cloud computing platforms offered by Google that help small to medium-sized businesses scale and grow. It’s a solid, secure set of cloud services that makes moving old apps into the cloud straightforward. With GCP, you can build, launch, and manage your apps and data in the cloud without a lot of hassle. It’s fast, flexible, and designed to help you keep up as your business changes.

Started in 2008, this cloud computing services software helps businesses with web and mobile applications, enterprise applications, big data and analytics, machine learning and AI, and others. This is budget-friendly, as it offers 15 GB of free storage, works with built-in security, and explores new ways to grow by modernizing applications.

It includes lift-and-shift as-is into the cloud, refactoring, and modernization of apps, which works by using tools like GCP’s Migrate for assessing apps and replicating to GCP.

After knowing the brief of AWS vs Azure vs GCP, if you want to get started with migration services and tools, you just have to sign up, choose your services, configure them, and then start building your applications with a data-driven and successful approach.

Quick Differences Between AWS vs Azure vs GCP

Since all three platforms offer internet-based computing services, let’s uncover the strengths and weaknesses of AWS vs Azure vs GCP that will help you make educated decisions for your business.

AspectsAzureAWSGCP
Scalability and performanceMicrosoft Azure has scalable infrastructure and a hybrid cloud to support enterprise workloads and applications.AWS has a variety of instance types and auto scaling to support different workloads and different amounts of traffic.GCP offers infrastructure and containerization capabilities for cloud-native applications and workloads.
Encryption and AuditsAzure is known to give a wide range of security features like end-to-end encryption, access, and compliance.AWS also offers an efficient and strong security framework, such as end-to-end encryption, access, and compliance.GCP provides security-centered solutions with encryption, security management, and compliance, all of which protect Google Cloud customers
Cost and pricingAzure offers a pricing scheme based on the pay-as-you-go model, with discounts offered for reserved instances and the use of a hybrid cloud.AWS provides the pricing model of pay-as-you-go with discounts for reserved instances and volume discounts.GCP provides a pay-as-you-go pricing plan, including discounts for sustained use and committed usage.
Integration and migration Services & ToolsMicrosoft Azure offers numerous migration tools and services, like Azure Migration Center and the Azure Database Migration Service.Amazon Web Services provides AWS Migration Hub and Amazon Database Migration Service.GCP also offers different tools and service options for data migration, including GCP Migration Center and GCP Database Migration Service.
Computer servicesThe main app migration services of Azure are Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Virtual Machines, and Azure Container Instances.On the other hand, AWS is going to do app migration with EC2, ECS, and EKS.Google will use Compute Engine, GKE, and App Engine for app migration.
StorageThe main Azure storage tools are Azure Blob Storage, Azure File Storage, and Azure Disk Storage.Similarly, the storage tools for AWS are Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, and Amazon EFS.The storage tools for GCP will be Google Cloud Datastore, Google Cloud Storage, and Google Cloud Filestore.
Process of App MigrationThe Azure migration process starts by assessing with Azure Migrate, then replicating, and finally testing to migrate while modernizing apps.For AWS, the app migration works by accessing the phase, replicating with AWS MGN, and then testing and cutting to migrate apps.The GCP migration strategies start by accessing the apps, planning, & choosing a migration strategy, deploying using the Migration Center, and then optimizing the migrated apps.

Which Legacy App Migration Cloud Platforms Are Best for You

The choice ofthe best legacy applications migration cloud platformswill depend on factors such as scalability, security, cost, and integration needs. AWS is ideal for large enterprises to manage complex workloads and applications. On the other hand, GCP is ideal for cloud-native application modernization and workload sharing, especially for those with a need to scale and containerize. Similarly, Azure is ideal for small and medium businesses that require a hybrid cloud environment with a Microsoft-friendly environment.
